record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg–de Vries equation and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time, in analogy with KAM-type persistence in finite-dimensional integrable systems?

evidence.quote: It is a natural, open and very challenging conjecture that the result of Damanik et al. remains true for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, i.e., for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, the Cauchy problem with (suitable) almost periodic initial data u0(x), has a unique global solution u(x, t), which evolves almost periodically in time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation
  ∂_t u(x,t) − 6 u(x,t) ∂_x u(x,t) + ∂_x^3 u(x,t) = 0,   (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ,
with initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x), where u_0 : ℝ → ℝ is almost periodic in the sense of Bohr (i.e., uniformly approximable by trigonometric polynomials). It is known that, for suitable classes of almost periodic initial data (for example, small analytic quasi-periodic data with Diophantine frequency vector, where the associated one-dimensional Schrödinger operator −∂_x^2 + u_0 has purely absolutely continuous spectrum that is not too thin), the Cauchy problem admits a unique global classical solution u(·,t) which, viewed as a curve in a suitable space of bounded continuous functions on ℝ, is almost periodic in t.

Now let P be a "suitable" perturbation of the KdV vector field (for instance, a Hamiltonian perturbation by a higher-order differential or local nonlinear term that preserves the natural energy/regularity structure), and consider the perturbed equation
  ∂_t u − 6 u ∂_x u + ∂_x^3 u = P(u, ∂_x u, ∂_x^2 u, …),   u(x,0) = u_0(x).

Question: For an appropriate class of such perturbations P and an appropriate class of almost periodic initial data u_0, does the Cauchy problem for the perturbed equation possess a unique global solution u(x,t) that, for each fixed x, is almost periodic in t (and, more strongly, is almost periodic as a curve into a function space) — in analogy with the KAM-type persistence of quasi-periodic motions in finite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian systems?
artifact.category_tag: Almost periodic solutions of perturbed KdV
artifact.status_search_result: The unperturbed almost-periodicity question (Deift's conjecture for KdV) has been established for small analytic quasi-periodic Diophantine data by Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic and related works. KAM theory for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV (Baldi–Berti–Montalto and others) yields existence of quasi-periodic-in-time solutions for special small initial data, but the Cauchy problem for perturbed KdV with general almost periodic initial data remains without local or global well-posedness results, and the analogue of the almost-periodicity result of Damanik et al. for perturbations of KdV is explicitly described in the literature as a natural and challenging open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Almost Periodicity in Time of Solutions of the KdV Equation (Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes almost periodicity in time of KdV solutions for small analytic quasi-periodic initial data with Diophantine frequency, proving Deift's conjecture in this setting (the unperturbed case).
status_evidence.claim: The base (unperturbed KdV) statement is proved only for restricted classes of almost periodic data.

status_evidence.title: KAM for autonomous quasi-linear perturbations of KdV (Baldi–Berti–Montalto)
status_evidence.snippet: Concerning the initial value problem for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV, there are no results even for the local existence theory. However, the initial conditions selected by the KAM theorem give rise to global-in-time solutions.
status_evidence.claim: For perturbations of KdV, the Cauchy problem with general almost periodic data is not understood; only special KAM tori are constructed.

status_evidence.title: KdV equation under periodic boundary conditions and its perturbations (Kuksin)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing persistence of finite-gap and quasi-periodic solutions under perturbations; perturbations of general almost periodic solutions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Persistence of almost periodic-in-time solutions for perturbed KdV is an open problem.
